text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: canary_slo_burn for service=redwood-gateway (canary pool) — SLO 99.9% p99 latency breach, starting 1m ago. Link: https://observability.redwood.example/alerts/INC-2031504321
Alex: saw this, I'm on it. Can anyone confirm if deploy 2026.3.15-frontend went to canary?
Maria: yes that deploy started ~2031503100, only 10% traffic to canary. I don't see obvious infra errors from the host side.
Julian: I'm seeing a spike in 5xxs from the gateway to the inference backends during the canary window. Quick tail: ``ERROR infer_client.go: timeout reading response status=502 body='EOF'``
Lee: prometheus query looks bad: ``sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",route="/v1/generate",env="prod"}[1m])) by (status)`` shows 5xx increased from 0.1% to 6% at canary start.
Alex: dashboard link in the alert goes 404 for the canary dashboard? I get "dash not found" — did we rename it in the dashboard drift cleanup?
Maria: ugh, I pushed a dashboard change yesterday, maybe I accidentally removed the canary tile. I'm reverting now but need confirmation on immediate mitigation.
oncall-bot: Incident channel auto-created: #incident-canary-slo-2031504321. Paging policy: mobile+email to SRE Rotation.
Julian: Customer impact check: monitoring shows increased request errors for a subset of tokens; downstream clients might see degraded responses. No broad data loss.
ProductOps: Customer-facing SRE: can we assess if any paying tenants hit failures? Any tenants with high traffic routed to canary?
Lee: quick lookup: ``labels_by_tenant(http_requests_total)`` — one tenant (acme-inc) has 40% of the canary load and shows p99 > 3s and 5xx spikes.
Alex: ok plan: 1) kill new-routing FF to stop canary routing to that tenant 2) rollback canary deploy if necessary 3) mute noisy canary alerts to avoid paging flood. Who can flip the kill?
Maria: I'm nearest to the FF console. Running safe-kill: ``POST /flags/kill new-routing`` — will post audit.
Maria: (after) done. audit: ``{flag: new-routing, actor: maria, ts: 2031504380, to: off}`` :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Feature flag change recorded. Rule: traffic routing will revert to stable pool for flag=new-routing.
Julian: after the kill, 5xx rate dropped from 6% -> 1.2% in the next 30s. p99 is trending down.
Alex: nice. Do we still need rollback? canary looked unstable only for acme-inc traffic. If kill stabilizes, we can hold rollback. Thoughts?
Lee: agree hold. But alerting is too noisy — canary alerts are firing on transient spikes. We should mute the canary alert group and add a temporary SLO burn dashboard for the release owners.
SRE Rotation: muting alerts for canary group for 30m now. Muted by: oncall @2031504402.
ProductOps: drafting a customer message for acme-inc: "We're investigating degraded generation latency. We've rolled back routing for a recent canary change and are monitoring. We'll follow up within 30 minutes." Want approval from Alex.
Alex: approve, send. Include escalation contact and incident channel link.
Maria: still seeing missing dashboard issue — the canary-specific dashboard tile was deleted; I'm restoring the tile from history and will pin it to the incident channel when back.
Julian: we should log the root signals for postmortem: 1) deploy introduced a routing path that increased load for a single tenant 2) dashboard drift removed canary observability 3) alerts were too sensitive and paged on transient spike.
Alex: agreed. Quick add: add a precooked query for tenant-level SLOs to the postmortem checklist so next deploy has tenant isolation checks.
ops-bot: Logged mitigation actions: FF_kill by Maria @2031504380, alerts_muted by SRE Rotation @2031504402, monitoring_check by Lee @2031504445.
SRE Rotation: passing to next oncall in 20m for observation. I'll add a Handoff note: "canary FF killed, alert mute until 2031506200, monitoring OK but watch p99 for acme-inc."
Alex: thumbs up. Please create an incident ticket and assign to infra+deploy team for follow-up (dashboard restore, traffic shaping change, alert tuning).
ProductOps: ticket created INC-2031504321 in Jira, assigned to infra-deploy, severity P2, ETA initial triage 60m.
Maria: restoring dashboard now — restored tile and pinned link to incident channel.
Lee: final check: post-mitigation p99 looks back under SLO at 99.95% for global traffic, acme-inc trending down but still slightly above for next 10m.
Alex: closing pager from rotation. Keep channel open for postmortem notes and customer updates.
oncall-bot: Pager cleared: canary_slo_burn resolved at 2031504515. Incident state: under investigation -> mitigated.
Julian: postmortem bullets incoming. I'll capture traces and a short timeline for the writeup.
SRE Rotation: handing off to next oncall @2031504520. Handoff message: "canary FF off, alerts muted, dashboards restored, acme-inc under watch."
